description: StatQuest's clear, exam-friendly walkthrough of how neural networks make decisions: nodes, activation functions, and training. Directly addresses IGCSE Topic 6.5 — no calculus required.

description: 7-part series (30 min total) building a neural network from scratch. Mathematically precise but visually accessible — excellent for students who found 3Blue1Brown intuitive and want the equations next.

description: StatQuest's clear, slow-paced breakdown of decision trees and random forests with real data examples. Most exam-relevant ML concept for CBSE and IGCSE students.
author: StatQuest

description: University-level explanation of the GPT architecture: tokens, embeddings, transformer blocks, softmax. Precise without being impenetrable — ideal bridge between 3Blue1Brown and Karpathy.

author: CBSE / NCERT

title: AI Agents Explained — What They Are and How They Work
description: What AI agents, tool use, RAG, and agentic loops actually mean. Explains the next phase of AI beyond chatbots — relevant for students interested in where the field is heading in 2025–2030.
author: IBM Technology

title: Google Colab — Getting Started (Student Guide)
description: Google Colab setup guide and first notebook walkthrough. Free GPU-enabled Python environment in the browser — the tool every student doing an AI project should use first. No local installation needed.

description: The definitive visual introduction to vectors, matrices, transformations, and eigenvectors — the mathematical backbone of every ML algorithm. 16-chapter playlist totalling ~3 hours. Any student aged 16+ doing AI seriously should start here.

title: Essence of Calculus — 3Blue1Brown
description: Visual intuition for derivatives, integrals, and the chain rule — the maths behind backpropagation. 12 chapters, ~3 hours. Complement to the linear algebra series for students who want to truly understand how models learn.

title: Natural Language Processing — Full Crash Course

title: HuggingFace NLP Course — Chapter 1
description: Hugging Face's official intro to NLP with Transformers: what the pipeline does, tokenizers, models, and fine-tuning. The gateway to using real pre-trained models. Ideal for students who have done basic Python and want to build something with language.

title: Hugging Face NLP Course — Full (Free)
description: Complete 9-chapter NLP course using the Transformers library: pipelines, tokenizers, datasets, fine-tuning, and deployment. The definitive free resource for students who want to build real NLP applications. Requires Python and basic ML knowledge.

title: How Stable Diffusion Works — Latent Diffusion Explained

author: Computerphile

title: Generative Adversarial Networks — GANs Explained
description: How GANs work: the generator and discriminator as adversaries, training dynamics, and applications from deepfakes to data augmentation. Essential for understanding a decade of generative AI history before diffusion took over.

title: The Turing Test — History and Philosophy
description: The origin and meaning of the Turing Test, Chinese Room argument, and what it means for a machine to think. Essential for IGCSE Topic 6.1, CBSE Unit 1, and IB philosophy of AI discussions.

title: Google Gemini — Multimodal AI Explained
description: How Gemini 1.5 processes text, images, audio, video, and code in one model. Covers the architectural leap from GPT-3 era to native multimodality. Students understand where the frontier actually is in 2024-25.

title: OpenAI o1: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in AI

author: AI Explained

title: AI Coding Tools in 2025 — Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code
description: Practical walkthrough of AI pair programming tools: autocomplete, chat-in-editor, agentic code generation. What they can do, what their limits are, and how to use them without losing your own skills.

title: Google NotebookLM for Students — Full Walkthrough
description: How to use Google NotebookLM: upload PDFs, textbooks, notes — get summaries, Q&A, audio overviews, and study guides. The single most useful AI study tool for students in 2024-25. Demonstrated with real academic material.

title: AI Research Tools for Students — Perplexity, Consensus, Elicit
description: How to use AI-powered research assistants for academic work: Perplexity for live search, Consensus for peer-reviewed evidence, Elicit for literature reviews. Critical digital literacy for students writing essays or project reports.
author: Mike and Matty

title: Superintelligence — Nick Bostrom
description: The foundational text of long-term AI risk thinking: what happens when AI surpasses human intelligence and what control problems arise. Controversial and demanding — essential for any student serious about AI safety debate.

title: The Hundred-Page Machine Learning Book — Andriy Burkov
description: The full ML canon compressed to 100 pages. Formally rigorous but written to be read. For students ages 17+ who want mathematical depth without committing to a full textbook. Free to read online.

title: Grokking Machine Learning — Luis Serrano
description: Intuition-first ML with hand-drawn diagrams and minimal prerequisites. Covers regression, classification, SVMs, and neural networks without heavy maths. Best print book for students aged 16-18 starting ML.
author: Luis Serrano

title: Life 3.0 — Max Tegmark
description: MIT physicist Max Tegmark explores what superintelligent AI means for the human future — jobs, war, law, values, consciousness. Accessible, scenario-based, and genuinely engaging for students 15+. The most-read popular AI futures book.
author: Max Tegmark

title: On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots — Bender et al.
description: The 2021 paper that coined the term stochastic parrot — the critique that large language models are sophisticated pattern matchers that cannot understand meaning. Important counterpoint to capability hype; cited in IB Digital Society and AI ethics discussions.
author: Bender, Gebru, McMillan-Major, Shmitchell

title: Sparks of Artificial General Intelligence — Microsoft Research
description: Microsoft Research's influential paper arguing GPT-4 shows early signs of AGI across diverse tasks. Heavily debated — good for teaching students how to read AI research claims critically and what AGI actually means.
author: Bubeck et al. (Microsoft Research)

title: AI for Education in India — Ministry of Education Initiative
description: India's Ministry of Education initiative on AI integration across schools: CBSE curriculum updates, state board rollout, teacher training roadmap, and National Digital Education Architecture. Essential context for teachers and school administrators.
author: Ministry of Education, India

title: Common Sense Education — AI in Schools: Practical Guidance
description: Common Sense Media's practical guide for teachers on classroom AI policy: what to allow, how to frame AI use for learning, how to redesign assessments for the AI age, and how to have the conversation with students and parents.
author: Common Sense Education

title: MIT Moral Machine — AI Ethics Interactive Experiment
description: MIT's crowdsourced experiment on autonomous vehicle ethics: who should a self-driving car sacrifice in unavoidable accidents? Interactive dilemmas drawn from trolley problem research. Use as a 15-minute classroom activity to open ethics discussions.
author: MIT Media Lab

title: The Hidden Environmental Cost of AI — Water, Energy, Carbon
description: MIT Technology Review investigation into the environmental footprint of training and running large AI models: water consumption, electricity, and carbon emissions. Concrete data for students writing about AI sustainability.
author: MIT Technology Review

title: How Teens Navigate AI — Pew Research Survey
description: Pew Research data on how teenagers aged 13-17 use, perceive, and worry about AI: awareness, usage patterns, trust, and concerns. Primary source for discussions on AI and youth.
author: Pew Research Center

title: AI4K12 — AI Project Rubrics and Lesson Plans
description: AI4K12 initiative's teacher resources: project rubrics, assessment frameworks, five big ideas in AI, and classroom activities graduated by age. Built specifically for K-12 educators integrating AI into any subject.
author: AI4K12 Initiative

title: Python + Pandas for AI — Google Colab Starter (CBSE)
description: Google's beginner Colab notebook for learning pandas data manipulation — the essential first step before any ML project. Works in-browser, no setup. Directly supports CBSE AI Code 843 Unit 5 project work.
author: Google

title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero — Karpathy Full Series
description: Karpathy's complete playlist: micrograd to makemore to nanoGPT. Build a functioning language model from first principles across 8 videos. The most respected self-contained deep learning curriculum available — for serious students aged 17+.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: The Pioneers of AI — McCarthy, Minsky, and the Dartmouth Conference
description: The founding story of AI as a field: 1956 Dartmouth Conference, symbolic AI, Minsky and McCarthy's vision, and why it took 60 years for the field to deliver on its promises.
author: Lex Fridman

title: Google PAIR Guidebook — Human-AI Interaction Design
description: Google's People and AI Research guidebook: practical principles for designing AI that works with humans rather than against them. Includes case studies on transparency, feedback, and error handling. Good IB IA source on responsible AI design.
author: Google PAIR

title: AI in Indian Healthcare — Diagnostics, TB Detection, Rural Access
description: How Indian startups and hospitals are using AI for TB detection, diabetic retinopathy screening, and extending diagnostic reach to tier-2/tier-3 cities. Real case studies with social impact framing — excellent for CBSE and IB ethics discussions set in Indian context.
author: NASSCOM Foundation

title: MIT: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
description: MIT's free course on tools CS students actually need but are never taught: command line, Git, scripting, debugging, and data wrangling. Prerequisite-level skills for any AI project — recommended before Kaggle or CS50 AI.
author: MIT CSAIL

title: State of AI 2025 — Sequoia Capital Analysis
description: Sequoia's annual analysis of where AI is commercially and technically in 2025: which applications are generating revenue, which remain speculative, and what the next wave looks like. Real-world grounding for students discussing AI's future.
author: Sequoia Capital

title: 50 AI Prompts Every Teacher Should Know
description: Practical prompt templates for teachers: lesson plan generation, differentiated instruction, rubric creation, parent email drafting, formative assessment design, and feedback. Demonstrated live with real classroom examples.
author: Matt Miller (Ditch That Textbook)

title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders — fast.ai
description: Jeremy Howard's landmark free course that teaches deep learning top-down: you build working image classifiers and NLP models in lesson 1, then gradually understand why they work. Opposite of the theory-first approach — proven to work with motivated students aged 17+ who know basic Python. Used by Kaggle grandmasters and researchers worldwide.
author: Jeremy Howard

title: Deep Learning — Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville (Free Online)
description: The authoritative MIT Press textbook on deep learning, freely available online. Covers the full mathematical foundation: linear algebra, probability, optimisation, feedforward networks, CNNs, RNNs, and generative models. The book that Elon Musk called 'the only comprehensive book on the subject.' For advanced students aged 18+ or teachers building curriculum.
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning — Bishop (Free PDF)
description: Christopher Bishop's classic textbook on probabilistic machine learning, officially free as a PDF from Microsoft Research. Covers Bayesian methods, SVMs, kernel methods, and graphical models — the rigorous statistical ML foundation that underpins modern AI. For advanced students and teachers wanting deep theory.
author: Christopher M. Bishop

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction — Sutton & Barto (Free)
description: The foundational RL textbook by Richard Sutton and Andrew Barto, fully free online. Covers the complete theory of reward-based learning: bandits, MDPs, Q-learning, policy gradients. Essential for understanding how AlphaGo, ChatGPT's RLHF training, and game-playing AI actually work.
author: Richard Sutton, Andrew Barto

title: Day of AI — MIT RAISE Free K-12 Curriculum
description: MIT RAISE's free, Creative Commons-licensed AI curriculum that has reached over 1 million students in 170+ countries. Hands-on lessons organised by age group covering how machines learn, bias in AI, ethics, data science, and climate change. Teachers get educator guides, ready-to-use slides, and free PD certification. 4,000+ teachers used it with 130,000+ students in India in 2024 alone.
author: MIT RAISE
duration: Full day to full year — flexible

title: IBM SkillsBuild — AI Fundamentals (Free with Badge)
description: IBM's free AI fundamentals course for students: covers NLP, computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, and chatbots. Earns a verifiable IBM digital badge on completion — meaningful credentialing for students aged 14–20 with no prerequisites. IBM has pledged to train 2 million learners in AI by 2026.
author: IBM

title: DataCamp Classrooms — Free Full Platform for Teachers & Students
description: DataCamp offers completely free premium access (630+ courses on AI, ML, Python, data science) to teachers and their students. Teachers apply as a DataCamp Classroom, then invite students aged 17+. Covers everything from Python basics to LLMs, machine learning, and data engineering. One of the most underused but highest-value free resources for schools.
author: DataCamp

title: Microsoft AI For Beginners — 24 Lessons, Full GitHub Curriculum
description: Microsoft's free open-source 12-week, 24-lesson AI curriculum on GitHub. Covers symbolic AI, neural networks, computer vision, NLP, and generative AI with Jupyter notebooks and assignments. Includes beginner-friendly examples: Hello AI World, image classifier, sentiment analysis — all with detailed comments.
author: Microsoft

title: Spinning Up in Deep RL — OpenAI
description: OpenAI's educational resource for learning deep reinforcement learning from scratch: RL terminology, algorithm theory, clean code implementations, and a guide to growing into an RL research role. The authoritative entry point for understanding how ChatGPT's RLHF training and game-playing AI (AlphaGo) actually work. For advanced students aged 18+.
author: OpenAI

title: AI for Everyone — Andrew Ng (DeepLearning.AI)
description: Andrew Ng's non-technical 6-hour course on AI for non-coders: what AI can and cannot do, building AI strategy, navigating societal impacts. Designed for business, policy, and non-STEM students. Ideal for teachers, school administrators, and students who want AI literacy without programming. Free to audit.
author: Andrew Ng

title: Hugging Face Deep Reinforcement Learning Course
description: Hugging Face's free hands-on RL course: trains agents to play video games, walk, and solve robotics tasks using Gymnasium. Earns a certificate. Covers Q-learning, deep Q-networks, and policy gradient — the same techniques behind RLHF. Pairs perfectly with Spinning Up for students aged 17+.
author: Hugging Face

title: Media Literacy in the Age of AI — Edutopia Teacher Guide
description: Edutopia's practical teacher guide on building media literacy alongside AI literacy. Includes classroom frameworks for teaching students to question AI-generated content, evaluate sources, and develop 'habits of awareness' that go beyond fact-checking. Published November 2025.
author: Edutopia

title: Machine Bias — ProPublica Investigation into Algorithmic Justice
description: ProPublica's landmark 2016 investigation showing that a widely-used criminal risk scoring algorithm was twice as likely to falsely flag Black defendants as high-risk. The single most cited case study on algorithmic bias. Essential reading for any AI ethics unit — proves the stakes with real data.
author: ProPublica

title: Gender Shades — MIT Media Lab Facial Recognition Bias Study
description: Joy Buolamwini's MIT study showing that commercial facial recognition systems from IBM, Microsoft, and Face++ had error rates up to 34% higher for dark-skinned women vs lighter-skinned men. Launched a global conversation on AI bias. Pairs naturally with the ProPublica investigation for ethics units.
author: Joy Buolamwini, Timnit Gebru

title: Coded Bias — Documentary on Algorithmic Discrimination
description: Netflix documentary following Joy Buolamwini and other researchers exposing bias in facial recognition and algorithmic decision-making used in hiring, banking, and policing. The most accessible and emotionally powerful introduction to AI bias for students aged 14+. Pairs with Gender Shades and ProPublica articles.
author: Shalini Kantayya (Director)

title: Ex Machina — Film for AI Consciousness and Ethics Discussion
description: Alex Garland's film about a programmer testing an AI's consciousness — explores the Turing Test, manipulation, what personhood means, and the ethics of creating thinking machines. Widely used in IB TOK and ethics classes. Suitable from age 15. Pair with the Turing Test TED-Ed video for a complete ethics lesson.
author: Alex Garland

title: What is ChatGPT Doing… and Why Does It Work? — Stephen Wolfram
description: Stephen Wolfram's extraordinarily detailed yet accessible explanation of how LLMs work from first principles: tokens, embeddings, attention, training, temperature. The single best long-form explanation of ChatGPT for a technically curious student. Takes 1–2 hours to read properly but fully worth it.
author: Stephen Wolfram

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models — OpenAI
description: The 2020 paper establishing that LLM performance scales predictably with compute, data, and model size. Explains why the industry has bet everything on making models bigger — and why that bet has largely worked. Essential context for understanding the GPT-3/4/Claude era.
author: Kaplan et al. (OpenAI)

title: Roboflow Learn — Computer Vision Projects for Students
description: Roboflow's free learning hub with step-by-step guides for building computer vision projects: object detection, image classification, pose estimation. Includes pre-labelled public datasets and free model training. The easiest way for a student to build a real CV project without collecting their own data.
author: Roboflow

title: Hugging Face Spaces — Explore and Deploy AI Apps for Free
description: Hugging Face's platform for discovering thousands of live AI demos: image generators, NLP models, speech recognition, code generation. Students can run real state-of-the-art models instantly in the browser, and publish their own projects for free. The best place to explore what AI can actually do today.
author: Hugging Face

title: Papers With Code — State-of-the-Art AI Research with Code
description: Tracks the latest AI research papers alongside their open-source implementations. Students can see exactly what the frontier of AI looks like right now, find code to reproduce results, and identify unsolved benchmarks. The best single site for advanced students who want to move from learning to doing.
author: Papers With Code

title: AI Now Institute Annual Report — Power, Policy, and Accountability
description: The AI Now Institute's annual research report on AI's social and political dimensions: corporate concentration, labour impacts, surveillance, and policy gaps. Stronger critical lens than the Stanford AI Index — excellent for IB students examining who controls AI and who bears its costs.
author: AI Now Institute

title: Two Minute Papers — AI Research Explained in 2 Minutes
description: Károly Zsolnai-Fehér explains recent AI research papers in 2–5 minute videos: image synthesis, physics simulation, reinforcement learning, robotics. Best channel for keeping up with where AI is going week by week. Perfect for students who want to stay current without reading full papers.
author: Károly Zsolnai-Fehér

title: Sentiment Analysis with Python — Full Beginner Project
description: Build a complete sentiment classifier from scratch: data loading, preprocessing, TF-IDF vectorisation, Naive Bayes, and evaluation. The ideal first real NLP project for a 16-year-old student — concrete, completable in one session, and genuinely teaches how text classification works.
author: freeCodeCamp

title: Convolutional Neural Networks — Stanford CS231n Lecture
description: Stanford's CS231n lecture on CNNs: convolution operations, feature maps, pooling, and architectures (AlexNet, VGG, ResNet). The university-level technical reference for how image recognition actually works. For advanced students aged 17+ who want the full picture.
author: Stanford / Fei-Fei Li

title: Turing Award Lecture — Bengio, Hinton, LeCun: Deep Learning
description: The 2018 ACM Turing Award winners — the three 'godfathers of deep learning' — discuss the history of neural networks from the 1980s to today: what they believed when no one else did, and what comes next. Primary source from the people who actually built modern AI.
author: Yann LeCun, Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio

title: Sam Altman on the Future of AI — Lex Fridman Podcast
description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discusses AGI timelines, safety concerns, GPT-4, and what he thinks about the future of intelligence. Primary source from the person leading the most influential AI lab in the world. Good for IB EE, debates on AI governance, and understanding how industry insiders think.
author: Lex Fridman

title: Geoffrey Hinton Leaves Google — On AI Risks and Regrets
description: Geoffrey Hinton, the godfather of deep learning, explains why he left Google in 2023 and what risks he is now worried about. A rare primary source of someone who built modern AI expressing genuine fear about where it's going. Essential for AI safety and ethics discussions.
author: BBC / CBS News

title: Train an AI to Play Snake — Python Beginner Project
description: Step-by-step project to build a reinforcement learning agent that learns to play the classic Snake game using PyTorch and Python. One of the most satisfying first AI projects: you can watch the agent get better in real time. GitHub tutorial with full code.
author: Patrick Loeber

title: Feature Visualization — What Does a Neural Network See? (Distill)
description: Distill.pub's interactive article showing what features neural networks actually learn to detect — from edges in early layers to complete objects in later ones. Beautifully illustrated, browser-interactive, and answers the question students always ask: what is going on inside the black box?
author: Olah et al. (Google Brain / Distill)

title: TensorFlow Playground — Build Neural Networks in Your Browser
description: Google's interactive in-browser neural network playground: drag, drop, and watch a neural network learn in real time. No code. Change layers, neurons, activation functions, and datasets and immediately see the effect. Best single tool for building intuition about how neural networks train — ideal for ages 14+.
author: Google

title: AI Hiring Tools Are Discriminating — Washington Post Investigation
description: Washington Post investigation into how AI hiring tools used by major companies systematically disadvantage certain candidates based on race, gender, and age — and why this matters for students entering the workforce in 2025+. Concrete case study of high-stakes algorithmic bias.
author: Washington Post

title: Python Machine Learning — Real Python Complete Guide
description: Real Python's comprehensive guide to ML in Python: data preprocessing, scikit-learn, model evaluation, and overfitting. Written for developers who want practical understanding — cleaner and more complete than most YouTube tutorials. The reference guide students should bookmark before starting any ML project.
author: Real Python

title: AI Safety Fundamentals — Alignment Curriculum (BlueDot Impact)
description: BlueDot Impact's free 8-week AI alignment curriculum: readings, discussions, and exercises used in university and professional courses globally. Covers deceptive alignment, reward hacking, scalable oversight, and governance. The most credible structured AI safety learning path for advanced students aged 18+ interested in the field.
author: BlueDot Impact

title: Attention and Augmented Recurrent Neural Networks — Distill
description: Distill.pub's beautifully illustrated explanation of attention mechanisms: how neural networks learn what to focus on. The conceptual foundation for transformers and every modern LLM. Interactive diagrams show exactly how attention scores work — the clearest visual explanation available.
author: Olah, Carter (Google Brain / Distill)

title: The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence — Luciano Floridi (ed.)
description: Oxford University Press anthology of landmark essays on AI ethics: privacy, autonomy, accountability, bias, and existential risk. Each essay is standalone and accessible — ideal for IB EE topic exploration, TOK discussions, or building a rigorous ethics reading list. Floridi is the EU's leading AI ethics philosopher.
author: Luciano Floridi (ed.)

title: Weapons of Math Destruction — Cathy O'Neil
description: Data scientist Cathy O'Neil shows how algorithms used in hiring, lending, policing, and education reinforce inequality rather than remove it. Written accessibly for a general audience — one of the best books for students aged 16+ to understand why AI bias is a systemic rather than technical problem.
author: Cathy O'Neil

title: Atlas of AI — Kate Crawford
description: Kate Crawford's investigation of AI's physical infrastructure: mines for rare earth metals, warehouse workers, data labellers, and surveillance systems. Makes visible the human and environmental costs that 'AI' obscures. Essential for students who want to think critically about who bears AI's costs.
author: Kate Crawford

title: Confusion Matrix, Precision, Recall, F1 — StatQuest
description: StatQuest's definitive walkthrough of model evaluation: confusion matrix (TP, FP, FN, TN), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score with worked examples. Slow-paced and visual — the clearest explanation available. Directly maps to CBSE Code 417 Class 10 Unit 3 (Evaluating Models) and Code 843 Class 11 Unit 6. Students who watch this once can answer any model evaluation exam question.
author: StatQuest

title: Orange Data Mining — Complete Beginner Tutorial
description: Step-by-step walkthrough of Orange Data Mining: importing data, building visual workflows, exploring datasets, and running classification models — all with no code. Directly maps to CBSE Code 417 Class 10 Unit 4 (Statistical Data). The 2025-26 official syllabus mandates Orange as the no-code AI tool for practical examination. Students must know this tool.
author: Orange Data Mining

title: WHO: Ethics and Governance of AI for Health
description: WHO's official guidance on AI ethics in healthcare — six core principles: transparency, inclusiveness, responsibility, impartiality, reliability, security and privacy. Directly maps to CBSE Class 10 Unit 1 Bioethics framework requirement (new in 2025-26 syllabus). Free, authoritative, accessible executive summary. Also strong IB Digital Society case study for Health context.
author: World Health Organization

title: Scikit-learn Complete Beginner Tutorial — Classification, Regression, Clustering
description: Hands-on scikit-learn walkthrough: train_test_split, linear regression, KNN classification, and K-means clustering with real datasets. Each concept under 10 minutes, with runnable code. Directly maps to CBSE Code 843 Class 11 Unit 6 practical requirements — the syllabus explicitly lists scikit-learn programs for regression, classification, and clustering. Students who work through this will be fully prepared for the practical exam.
author: Sentdex

title: Build a Chatbot — Google Dialogflow Quickstart
description: Google's official Dialogflow quickstart: create, train, and test a conversational AI agent in the browser with no advanced coding. Directly maps to the CBSE Code 843 Class 11 practical requirement to build a chatbot (explicitly listed in the official syllabus). Free tier, no install required. Students can complete the chatbot activity in a single lab session.
author: Google Cloud

title: Expert Systems Explained — IGCSE Computer Science 0478
description: Exam-focused explanation of expert systems: knowledge base, inference engine, user interface, explanation facility, and rule-based reasoning — with a worked IGCSE 6-mark answer. The most frequently examined IGCSE 0478 AI topic. Cambridge examiner reports consistently flag students losing marks by not naming the inference engine specifically. After this video students can answer any expert systems question on Paper 1.
author: Craig'n'Dave

title: Automated Systems and Robotics — IGCSE Computer Science 0478
description: IGCSE-targeted explanation of automated systems (sensors, microprocessors, actuators) and robotics: how robots are defined, types (industrial, surgical, domestic), and a complete advantages/disadvantages breakdown for 6-mark exam answers. Examiner reports show Sections 6.1 and 6.2 are among the most common sources of dropped marks. Covers both the 2023-2025 and 2026-2028 syllabus versions.
author: Craig'n'Dave

title: IGCSE 0478 AI and Robotics — Examiner-Report Study Notes
description: Tutopiya's examiner-report-based study notes for IGCSE 0478 Section 6: exact keywords the mark scheme credits, common student mistakes flagged by Cambridge examiners 2022–2024, and model 6-mark answers for automated systems, robotics, and AI. Mapped to the 2026-2028 syllabus. The most practical exam-prep resource for IGCSE AI topics — especially useful for understanding what Cambridge actually awards marks for.
author: Tutopiya

title: Craig'n'Dave — IGCSE Computer Science 0478 Complete Channel
description: The gold-standard free resource for IGCSE Computer Science 0478. Every topic covered with exam-focused explanations, mark-scheme walkthroughs, and past paper analysis. Their Section 6 playlist covers automated systems, robotics, expert systems, and machine learning with IGCSE precision — including the exact terminology Cambridge examiners credit. Recommended as the primary exam-prep channel for all IGCSE students.
author: Craig'n'Dave

title: EU AI Act Explained — European Parliament
description: The European Parliament's official explainer on the EU AI Act (2024): risk-based categories from 'unacceptable risk' (banned) to 'minimal risk', transparency requirements for generative AI, enforcement mechanisms, and global implications. Primary source for IB Digital Society content 3.6 (AI governance). Strong Paper 1, Paper 2, and IA case study material. Also relevant to IGCSE ethical impacts.
author: European Parliament

title: IB Digital Society IA Guide 2026 — Structure, Tips and Examiner Expectations
description: Step-by-step guide to the IB Digital Society Internal Assessment (Inquiry Project): how to form a research question using AO3 command terms (evaluate, discuss, to what extent), connect IB concepts (Power, Privacy, Identity), structure the Inquiry Process Document, build evidence-based analysis, and present the Multimedia Presentation. The IA accounts for 25% of SL and 20% of HL grade — every IB student should read this before starting.
author: TutorsPlus

title: Facial Recognition Is Everywhere and Barely Regulated — MIT Technology Review
description: MIT Technology Review investigation into the global spread of facial recognition: accuracy gaps by race and gender, state surveillance, corporate deployment, and near-total regulatory absence. One of the strongest IB Digital Society case studies connecting AI (content 3.5) directly to the Identity, Privacy, and Power concepts. Suitable for Paper 1 source-based inquiry, Paper 2 source evaluation, and IA investigations.
author: MIT Technology Review

title: Autonomous Weapons Systems — ICRC Position and Analysis
description: The International Committee of the Red Cross's position paper on lethal autonomous weapons (LAWS): definition, legal accountability gaps under international humanitarian law, IHL compliance challenges, and calls for binding regulation. Primary source for IB HL Extension — Governance and Human Rights challenge topic. Directly connects AI content (3.7 Robots) to concepts of Power and Values and Ethics. Strong HL Paper 3 material.
author: International Committee of the Red Cross

title: IB Digital Society Hub — Case Studies, IA Templates, HL Resources
description: The leading independent resource hub for IB Digital Society: concept-mapped case studies for AI, surveillance, media, and governance topics; IA and EE templates updated for 2025-26; HL Extension inquiry materials on governance, human rights, and sustainable development; past paper walkthroughs. Equivalent to Revision Village for this subject. All content aligned to the official subject guide (first assessment 2024).
author: IB Digital Society Educators

title: How Diffusion Models Work — Stable Diffusion Explained
description: Computerphile's clear visual explanation of how diffusion models generate images: forward diffusion (adding noise step by step), reverse diffusion (learned denoising), and how text prompts guide the process via CLIP embeddings. The mechanism behind Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, and DALL-E. Essential for generative AI literacy now expected across all boards. Suitable for CBSE Unit 4, IGCSE Section 6.3, and IB content 3.3.
author: Computerphile

title: IEA: AI Data Centres and Global Energy Demand (Electricity 2024)
description: The International Energy Agency's 2024 analysis of AI and data centre electricity consumption — projects data centres will consume electricity equivalent to Japan's entire usage by 2026. Primary source for discussing AI's environmental cost. Credible for IB HL Sustainable Development extension, CBSE AI ethics / SDG units, and IGCSE ethical impacts. High authority: government-backed, free, data-rich.
author: International Energy Agency

title: Yann LeCun on the Future of AI — Lex Fridman Podcast
description: Lex Fridman interviews Yann LeCun (Meta AI Chief Scientist, Turing Award winner) on why LLMs are not sufficient for AGI, autonomous AI systems, open-source vs closed AI, and what genuine machine understanding might require. The first 45 minutes stand alone as a discussion of foundational questions. Ideal for IB extended essay background, CBSE AI research projects, and any engaged student wanting expert-level perspective.
author: Lex Fridman

title: e-Pathshala — NCERT AI and CS Content (Offline App)
description: NCERT's official e-Pathshala portal: access Class 11-12 Computer Science textbooks, videos, and interactive content — offline via the free e-Pathshala app (Android and iOS). AI chapters 16-18 available in both Hindi and English. Critical for RBSE students with limited internet connectivity — content downloads for offline use and is 100% aligned to Rajasthan board examination requirements. Also useful for CBSE Hindi-medium students.
author: NCERT / Ministry of Education
